I've opened an issue in their GitHub (https://github.com/tlocke/pg8000/issues/81), and think this modification should be done in SQLAlchemy.

My use case is exactly the same as @leandropls 's one:
I request a token for the password, but the token is only valid for 1 hour:
```python
class ApplicationDefaultTokenPassword(object):
    # set un instance of this class as database password
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.token = None
        self.expiry = None

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        if self.token is None or self.expiry < datetime.utcnow():
            scopes = ['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform']
            credentials, _  = default_credentials(scopes=scopes)
            request = requests.Request()
            credentials.refresh(request)
            self.token = credentials.token
            self.expiry = credentials.expiry
        
        return self.token

```

we do test this, but each dialect should handle this manually in `connect` since there is no other call that receives the connection arguments at each connection.

I'm inclined to suggest just updating the documentation to suggest subclassing string when providing a custom class. Otherwise custom dialect may or may not work. I don't think adding another function call to the connection flow is warranted in this case

@leandropls @francois-gay  would subclassing str in your use cases solve this issue? (so using `class DynamicPassword(str):` and `class ApplicationDefaultTokenPassword(str):`
I don't see how this would work, since str is immutable.

A subclass is not:

```py
class MyStr(str):
    def __init__(self):
        self.c = 0

    def __str__(self):
        self.c += 1
        return f"v={self.c}"

    __repr__ = __str__


s = MyStr()
print(s, s, s, s)
```
outputs `v=1 v=2 v=3 v=4`

I'm traveling and don't have time to look but it should absolutely be possible for the defaultdialect to be adjusted in this way as well as to provide a suite test to ensure all dialects do the right thing.  I would not be in favor of subclassing string as that's an unusual and awkward pattern.
